**Notes from what I did read**

Source: Gill's Exposition, Genesis 37 — https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/genesis/37.htm

- **Introduction:** Gill says the story of Joseph starts in this chapter, and the rest of Genesis is mostly about him. The first thing the chapter tells is his brothers' hatred of him. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/genesis/37.htm)
- **v. 1:** Gill reads this verse against the end of chapter 36. Esau's family lived in their land as owners and lords. Jacob, like his father before him, lived in Canaan as a stranger and visitor. Gill suggests reading it as "*but* Jacob dwelt…" to bring out that contrast. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/genesis/37.htm)
- **v. 2:** Gill names the brothers Joseph worked with: Dan and Naphtali (Bilhah's sons) and Gad and Asher (Zilpah's sons). He thinks Jacob chose to put Joseph with them rather than with Leah's sons. Bilhah had been the maid of Joseph's dead mother Rachel, so her sons might be expected to treat Joseph best. Gill says Joseph reported them because he couldn't put up with their wrongdoing. The excerpt cut off there. (https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/genesis/37.htm)
